findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The serializer defines the conditional-attribute hook as `include_website_name` (no trailing `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializer's conditional inclusion hook is `include_#{attr}?`, so this method is never invoked and `website_name` is serialized (as null) for every user regardless of the guard. No user-visible breakage (templates test truthiness of website_name, so null is handled), but the guard is dead code: a future developer editing `include_website_name` to change serialization behavior will see no effect, and every user payload carries a null website_name key. The rest of the Discourse serializer codebase uses the question-mark form, so this reads as an assumed framework contract that does not hold.

[BUG] The sibling-domain matching in website_name treats any two hostnames that share a trailing dot-label sequence as the same domain, so unrelated sites on multi-part public suffixes (e.g. instance at forum.example.co.uk, user website at other.co.uk) are rendered with their full URL path. On any instance whose hostname has 3+ labels under a public suffix (co.uk, com.au, github.io, web.app), a user whose website is a completely unrelated sibling domain (other.co.uk/page vs forum.example.co.uk) gets website_name = 'other.co.uk/page' instead of just 'other.co.uk' — the elsif branch compares host.split('.')[1..-1] ('co.uk' == 'co.uk') and the else branch matches via ends_with?("." << website_host), both firing on public-suffix coincidences; the output contradicts the PR's own acceptance criterion ('website domain is same as instance domain') and misleads users into reading an external link as an internal one. The added spec only tests one registrable-domain shape (example.com/forums.example.com), so the over-match ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new spec exercises only the exact-match branch and the else branch of website_name; the elsif sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, the one the code comment documents) has no test case anywhere in the diff. A regression in the elsif branch (e.g. someone 'simplifies' the split('.')[1..-1] comparison) passes the full suite silently, and the documented 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' behavior — the branch most likely to be broken by the public-suffix fix this code needs — is the only untested one.

[ADVISORY] website_name concatenates URI(...).path unconditionally, so 'http://example.com' renders as 'example.com' while 'http://example.com/' renders as 'example.com/' for the identical site. Two users pointing at the same homepage see inconsistent display depending solely on whether their stored URL has a trailing slash; the same-host branch should strip a lone '/' path before concatenating.

[BUG] The stated invariant 'show full path when website domain is same as instance domain' is not enforced for the most common 'www.' pairing: with instance host `example.com` (2 labels) and website `http://www.example.com/user`, the elsif is skipped (3 != 2 labels) and the else branch's `ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so website_name returns the bare host `www.example.com`. On root-domain Discourse instances, a website that is the www alias of the instance domain shows only the hostname while the identical pairing on a subdomain instance (`forums.example.com` + `www.example.com`) shows the full path — two instances of the same site get visibly inconsistent treatment for the exact case the PR title claims to fix.

[BUG] The `websiteName` computed property is deleted here, but this diff migrates only templates/user/user.hbs to `model.website_name` — any other template that consumed `websiteName` from this controller context (notably the user card template) now resolves it to undefined, so its `{{#if websiteName}}` block stops rendering the website link entirely. After this change the user card (the other primary surface that displays a user's website name) silently loses or desyncs its website display: the removal is a half-migration that leaves at least one in-tree consumer of the deleted property broken or pinned to the old behavior.

[ADVISORY] The requirement states one rule ('same as instance domain') but the implementation ships three undocumented heuristics — exact host match, equal-label-count registrable-suffix match, and parent-domain match — whose semantics are defined only by the tests added in this same PR, with no traceability to a stated requirement or setting to constrain them. Instance operators get behavior they never asked for: on `talk.example.org`, a user linking `http://shop.example.org/item` (a different site) now displays the full path `shop.example.org/item`, and because this is server-side serializer logic with no toggle, the only way to revert to the stated 'same domain only' behavior is a code change; future maintainers must reverse-engineer the intended semantics from inline comments.

[ADVISORY] The new tests cover only three of the four code paths in `website_name` — the elsif branch (`www.example.com == forum.example.com`, equal label counts > 2) has no test in this diff. A regression in the 13-line ternary on line 146 (the most convoluted branch, doing a double split/join comparison) ships silently: no failing test would catch a typo in `[1..-1]`, a swapped operand, or the `> 2` guard being dropped, and the inconsistency reported above for the adjacent branches is exactly the kind of defect this missing case would have surfaced.

[ADVISORY] `include_website_name` is dead weight: it returns true whenever `website` is present, but the template gates on `{{#if model.website_name}}` and `website_name` already returns nil when the host cannot be parsed, so the inclusion hook provides no guarantee its name implies and changes no observable behavior. The next maintainer reading `include_website_name` reasonably assumes it guarantees `website_name` is non-nil whenever included — it does not (a malformed website passes the hook yet yields nil) — so the misleading guard must be traced and reasoned about on every future edit to this serializer; deleting it removes one place-to-update with zero behavior change.

[BUG] Deleting the `websiteName` computed property from UserController leaves every other template that binds `{{websiteName}}` — notably the user-card template (templates/user/card.hbs), which renders the website row from the same controller context — resolving against a now-nonexistent property. Ember resolves the missing `websiteName` binding to undefined, so `{{#if websiteName}}` in the user card evaluates false and the website/globe row silently disappears from every user card, while the profile page (the only template updated in this diff) keeps working — a regression that ships green because the touched template's behavior is unchanged.

[ADVISORY] The new specs cover only branch 1 (exact host equality) and branch 3 (parent-domain suffix) of `website_name`; the middle branch — equal label counts > 2 with matching suffixes after the first label, e.g. website www.example.com against instance forum.example.com — has no test in this diff. A regression in that branch's index arithmetic (`split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`) or its label-count guard ships unnoticed, silently changing how subdomain-matched websites are labeled for every user whose site is a sibling subdomain of the forum.

[ADVISORY] `website_name` parses `URI(website.to_s)` twice and recomputes `website_host.split('.')`/`discourse_host.split('.')` up to four times across the branch conditions instead of binding them once. The method runs per user on list-shaped serialization paths (user cards, directory), so each render pays redundant URI parsing and array splits; the next editor who adds a fourth branch must re-duplicate the same split/parse expressions, growing the divergence surface.

[ADVISORY] The branch-3 check `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is a bare string-suffix match with no registrable-domain/public-suffix awareness, so any website host that happens to be a string suffix of the forum host's parent chain qualifies as 'same domain'. A user who sets their website to a bare-suffix host (e.g. http://co.uk/ against a forum at forums.example.co.uk, or http://com/ against example.com) gets their link labeled with that bare host plus the URL path, making an unrelated external site display as if it were an in-instance path; the displayed label then disagrees with the actual `href` destination.

[ADVISORY] The client-side `websiteName` computed property is deleted but only one of its consumers (user/user.hbs) is migrated to `model.website_name` in this diff, making the removal a silent public-surface change for any remaining template that binds `websiteName`. Any other template or component that still renders `{{websiteName}}` (the property was publicly exposed on the user controller and was even documented in the model's JSDoc, which this diff edits) now silently renders an empty profile website line with no error, and only a manual template audit catches it; the follow-up breakage surfaces as a blank UI, not a failing test.

[ADVISORY] The shipped behavior is broader and asymmetric relative to the stated contract 'show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain': a website that is a subdomain of the instance domain (e.g. website http://blog.example.com/x on a forum at example.com) falls to the else branch and shows the bare host, while a parent-domain website (http://example.com/x on forum.example.com) and equal-label-count sibling subdomains get the full path. Users whose website is a subdomain of the forum's own domain get the truncated display the feature was meant to eliminate, while users on parent/sibling domains get the full path — so the visible rule on a live forum is inconsistent and unexplainable from the PR's stated contract; the spec suite only encodes the three covered cases and nothing pins the subdomain-of-instance case, so any future refactor of these branches can flip it silently.

[ADVISORY] `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any stored website value URI cannot resolve a host from (e.g. a schemeless value like 'www.example.com'), making `website_name` nil so the entire website block (globe icon plus link) disappears from the profile even though `website` is present and `include_website_name` returns true. A user whose saved website value yields no URI host loses their website display entirely with no error and no test coverage — the new spec cases only exercise well-formed 'http://' URLs, so a regression or normalization change in what gets stored in user_profile.website shows up only as vanished profile links in production.

[ADVISORY] The host comparisons in website_name are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI#host preserves the case exactly as written in the user-supplied website URL, so a host stored as 'Example.com' never matches the lowercase Discourse.current_hostname. A user whose profile website is entered with any uppercase character in the host (e.g. 'http://Example.com/user' on the forum's own domain) fails the website_host == discourse_host check and the suffix checks, so the feature this PR exists to deliver (showing the full path for same-domain websites) silently does not apply for those users; the displayed name drifts from what the same user sees with a lowercase URL. Who gets bitten: legitimate same-domain users with capitalized URLs; a staff reviewer verifying the feature will see inconsistent behavior. (This is the canonical-form half of a normalization mismatch: the comparison input is not downcased before being compared against a lowercase canonical host — Discourse.current_hostname is always lowercase.) Fix is mechanical: compare website_host.downcase (or URI#hostname) against discourse_host.

[ADVISORY] The new 'has a website name' context never exercises the equal-length-multi-label branch of UserSerializer#website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 144-146: `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && > 2`), covering neither its match path (www.example.com website on a forum.example.com instance, which the code comment explicitly claims to handle) nor its mismatch path (equal-length hosts with different domains, which returns the bare host without the path). The most intricate comparison logic in the new method — the `[1..-1].join('.')` suffix comparison — ships with zero coverage; a regression there (e.g. an off-by-one in the split index, or comparing the wrong slices) would pass CI silently and only surface when a user's website is a sibling subdomain of the instance, showing the wrong link text.

[ADVISORY] The `include_website_name` guard (which omits :website_name when website is blank) is a new behavior-bearing attribute conditional with no assertion in the diff — website_name is a symbol introduced in this diff, so any test asserting its omission must exist in this diff, and the three added examples all set a website and only assert the present case. A regression that makes the serializer emit website_name: null (or emit the key when website is blank, e.g. returning a non-nil value from website_name for an empty website) would not be caught; template rendering `{{#if model.website_name}}` would silently hide or mis-render the website row for users with no website set.

[ADVISORY] No test exercises the `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` failure path — a website stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user', which URI.parse rejects) makes website_host nil and website_name return nil even though the :website attribute is serialized. A user whose profile website lacks a scheme gets :website present but :website_name omitted, so the entire globe/link block in templates/user/user.hbs ({{#if model.website_name}}) disappears — and since all three new spec examples use well-formed 'http://...' URLs, a change to the rescue or nil-handling would regress this with no failing test.

[BUG] website_name returns nil for website values that URI.parse rejects (e.g. legacy data like 'http://exa mple.com/x'), silently hiding the entire globe/link block in user.hbs, whereas the removed client-side code (website.split("/")[2]) still displayed a host for those same values. Any existing profile whose website string is not URI-parseable loses its displayed website link with no error and no log — a silent display regression for legacy data; users with malformed saved websites see the field vanish after deploy.

[BUG] The same-site detection is asymmetric: a website on a subdomain of a 2-label instance host (website 'www.example.com', Discourse.current_hostname 'example.com') falls into the else branch, ends_with?(".www.example.com") is false, and the path is dropped, while the mirrored configuration (instance 'forum.example.com', website 'www.example.com') shows the full path via the elsif branch. Users whose site is served at the apex domain get the truncated host-only display for subdomain websites even though the feature's stated purpose ('show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain') and the sibling 3-label case both say the path should be shown — the same logical site renders differently depending on which side holds the subdomain.

[ADVISORY] The new tests only exercise the website_host == discourse_host branch and the else (ends_with?) branch; the elsif branch (equal label counts > 2, e.g. instance 'forums.example.com' with website 'www.example.com') is never covered. The most convoluted conditional in website_name (the ternary comparing both split('.')[1..-1] suffixes) can regress to always-true or always-false without any test failing, and given the asymmetry bug at serializer lines 141-148 the branch boundary behavior is exactly where a regression is likely.

[ADVISORY] website_name re-parses URI(website.to_s) three times and re-splits both hosts up to three times inside one method, instead of parsing once into a local and deriving host/path/suffixes from it. The next person touching the same-site comparison logic must keep three independent URI parses and two sets of split('.') calls consistent with each other; a change to one parse site (e.g. adding scheme normalization) silently diverges from the other two, which is exactly how the label-count asymmetry crept in.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

If the framework expects the `?` form, this method will not be called and `website_name` will be emitted for all users (often as null), making the guard effectively dead code. This is grounded in the method name mismatch shown in the diff, though the exact serializer hook contract isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

This will incorrectly treat hosts like `forum.co.uk` and `other.co.uk` (or any two `*.co.uk`-style hosts with the same label count) as the same “domain” because both remainders become `co.uk`, causing it to return `website_host + path` (full path) when it should likely return just the host. The spec added only covers `example.com` vs `forums.example.com` and doesn’t exercise multi-part public suffix cases, so this edge-case defect would ship unverified. (The finding’s specific `forum.example.co.uk` vs `other.co.uk` example doesn’t trigger the `elsif`, but the underlying public-suffix overmatch is real in the `elsif` logic.)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` with three paths: `website_host == discourse_host`, an `elsif` for “sibling subdomain” (`(split('.').length == ...) && > 2`), and a final `else`. The added specs cover the equality branch (`current_hostname = 'example.com'`) and the final `else` branch (`'discourse.org'` and `'forums.example.com'` both route to `else` because domain-part lengths are not both >2 and equal in the first case, and lengths differ in the third case). There is no test for the `elsif` scenario like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` where both have length 3 and share the parent domain. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test risk for the newly added logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, when `website_host == discourse_host` (and in other branches that append the path), it concatenates `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` without normalizing the path. In Ruby, `URI('http://example.com').path` is typically `""` while `URI('http://example.com/').path` is `"/"`, so two equivalent homepage URLs will render differently (`example.com` vs `example.com/`) solely due to a trailing slash. This user-visible inconsistency is introduced by the new serializer logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` does behave as described for the `www` alias case: with `Discourse.current_hostname == 'example.com'` and `website_host == 'www.example.com'`, it falls through to the `else` and returns only `website_host` (no path) because `ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false. With a subdomain instance like `forums.example.com`, the `elsif` branch would include the path for `www.example.com`. This is a real, diff-grounded edge case/inconsistency in the newly added domain-matching logic, but it’s not clearly a verifiable defect against an explicit requirement in the diff (the specs only assert behavior for exact-match and parent-domain cases, not `www` alias handling).

So the include-hook does not guarantee the attribute will be non-nil, and its name can mislead maintainers into assuming it does. The added specs cover (1) via `current_hostname == 'example.com'` and (3) via `current_hostname == 'forums.example.com'` with `website_host == 'example.com'`. There is no spec exercising branch (2) (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so regressions in that sibling-subdomain logic could ship without test coverage.

It also repeatedly calls `website_host.split('.')` and `discourse_host.split('.')` within conditional expressions. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern (redundant parsing/splitting) rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The branch-3 check `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is a bare string-suffix match with no registrable-domain/public-suffix awareness, so any website host that happens to be a string suffix of the forum host's parent chain qualifies as 'same domain'. A user who sets their website to a bare-suffix host (e.g. http://co.uk/ against a forum at forums.example.co.uk, or http://com/ against example.com) gets their link labeled with that bare host plus the URL path, making an unrelated external site display as if it were an in-instance path; the displayed label then disagrees with the actual `href` destination.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branch-3 condition `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is a plain string-suffix check (no public-suffix/registrable-domain logic). From the diff, if the forum host is `forums.example.co.uk` and a user’s `website` host parses as `co.uk` (or similarly `com` vs `example.com`), this condition will be true and the serializer will return `website_host + URI(...).path` (e.g. `co.uk/user`), treating a bare suffix as if it were a parent domain match. This yields an incorrect `website_name` for such inputs, and the behavior is directly introduced by the new serializer logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side `websiteName` computed property is deleted but only one of its consumers (user/user.hbs) is migrated to `model.website_name` in this diff, making the removal a silent public-surface change for any remaining template that binds `websiteName`. Any other template or component that still renders `{{websiteName}}` (the property was publicly exposed on the user controller and was even documented in the model's JSDoc, which this diff edits) now silently renders an empty profile website line with no error, and only a manual template audit catches it; the follow-up breakage surfaces as a blank UI, not a failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `websiteName` removed from `controllers/user.js.es6` and the only shown consumer (`templates/user/user.hbs`) updated to use `model.website_name`. The finding’s core claim—that there are other remaining templates/components binding `{{websiteName}}` causing silent breakage—cannot be verified from the provided diff alone, since no other usages are shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shipped behavior is broader and asymmetric relative to the stated contract 'show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain': a website that is a subdomain of the instance domain (e.g. website http://blog.example.com/x on a forum at example.com) falls to the else branch and shows the bare host, while a parent-domain website (http://example.com/x on forum.example.com) and equal-label-count sibling subdomains get the full path. Users whose website is a subdomain of the forum's own domain get the truncated display the feature was meant to eliminate, while users on parent/sibling domains get the full path — so the visible rule on a live forum is inconsistent and unexplainable from the PR's stated contract; the spec suite only encodes the three covered cases and nothing pins the subdomain-of-instance case, so any future refactor of these branches can flip it silently.

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` is nontrivial and explicitly treats equality, “same-label-count sibling subdomains”, and “website is parent of instance domain” (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`) differently. From the diff, a website that is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. `website_host = blog.example.com`, `discourse_host = example.com`) falls into the final `else` and returns only `website_host` (no `+ URI(...).path`), while parent/sibling cases do return host+path. The added specs cover only the three implemented cases and do not pin the subdomain-of-instance behavior, so the edge-case/asymmetry the finding describes is real and diff-grounded, but it’s not provably a correctness defect without an explicit contract in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any stored website value URI cannot resolve a host from (e.g. a schemeless value like 'www.example.com'), making `website_name` nil so the entire website block (globe icon plus link) disappears from the profile even though `website` is present and `include_website_name` returns true. A user whose saved website value yields no URI host loses their website display entirely with no error and no test coverage — the new spec cases only exercise well-formed 'http://' URLs, so a regression or normalization change in what gets stored in user_profile.website shows up only as vanished profile links in production.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will indeed yield `nil` for inputs like `"www.example.com"` (no scheme), while `include_website_name` is gated only by `website.present?`. The template now shows the website UI only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present-but-unparseable website string would not be displayed. The added specs only cover `http://...` URLs, so this edge case is untested. However, the diff doesn’t prove such schemeless values can be stored (and the prior client-side `websiteName` extraction via `split('/')[2]` would also have hidden schemeless values), so it’s better classified as an uncovered edge-case/robustness concern rather than a definite new defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host comparisons in website_name are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI#host preserves the case exactly as written in the user-supplied website URL, so a host stored as 'Example.com' never matches the lowercase Discourse.current_hostname. A user whose profile website is entered with any uppercase character in the host (e.g. 'http://Example.com/user' on the forum's own domain) fails the website_host == discourse_host check and the suffix checks, so the feature this PR exists to deliver (showing the full path for same-domain websites) silently does not apply for those users; the displayed name drifts from what the same user sees with a lowercase URL. Who gets bitten: legitimate same-domain users with capitalized URLs; a staff reviewer verifying the feature will see inconsistent behavior. (This is the canonical-form half of a normalization mismatch: the comparison input is not downcased before being compared against a lowercase canonical host — Discourse.current_hostname is always lowercase.) Fix is mechanical: compare website_host.downcase (or URI#hostname) against discourse_host.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` is compared to `Discourse.current_hostname` using case-sensitive string equality and suffix logic, and the code does not normalize (`downcase`) either side before comparing. If `URI(...).host` can retain mixed-case from user input, same-domain URLs with uppercase characters would fail the `website_host == discourse_host` and related checks, so the intended “show full path for same-domain” behavior would not apply for those users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'has a website name' context never exercises the equal-length-multi-label branch of UserSerializer#website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 144-146: `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && > 2`), covering neither its match path (www.example.com website on a forum.example.com instance, which the code comment explicitly claims to handle) nor its mismatch path (equal-length hosts with different domains, which returns the bare host without the path). The most intricate comparison logic in the new method — the `[1..-1].join('.')` suffix comparison — ships with zero coverage; a regression there (e.g. an off-by-one in the split index, or comparing the wrong slices) would pass CI silently and only surface when a user's website is a sibling subdomain of the instance, showing the wrong link text.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: the added specs only stub `current_hostname` as `discourse.org` (2 labels), `example.com` (2 labels, hits `website_host == discourse_host`), and `forums.example.com` (3 labels vs website 2 labels, hits the final `ends_with?` branch). None of them can enter the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && ... > 2` branch in `UserSerializer#website_name`, so the suffix comparison `split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` is untested, including both its match and mismatch outcomes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `include_website_name` guard (which omits :website_name when website is blank) is a new behavior-bearing attribute conditional with no assertion in the diff — website_name is a symbol introduced in this diff, so any test asserting its omission must exist in this diff, and the three added examples all set a website and only assert the present case. A regression that makes the serializer emit website_name: null (or emit the key when website is blank, e.g. returning a non-nil value from website_name for an empty website) would not be caught; template rendering `{{#if model.website_name}}` would silently hide or mis-render the website row for users with no website set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new conditional serializer attribute via `include_website_name` (only include when `website.present?`) alongside new nontrivial `website_name` logic, but the added spec coverage only asserts cases where `user.user_profile.website` is set and never asserts omission/absence when the website is blank. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap around the new behavior-bearing guard rather than a proven functional defect in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test exercises the `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` failure path — a website stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user', which URI.parse rejects) makes website_host nil and website_name return nil even though the :website attribute is serialized. A user whose profile website lacks a scheme gets :website present but :website_name omitted, so the entire globe/link block in templates/user/user.hbs ({{#if model.website_name}}) disappears — and since all three new spec examples use well-formed 'http://...' URLs, a change to the rescue or nil-handling would regress this with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new server-side `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` that depends on `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early when `website_host.nil?` (so `website_name` can be omitted even when `website` is present via `include_website_name`). The template was changed to render the globe/link only when `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so this edge case affects UI output. The added specs only cover well-formed `http://...` URLs and do not exercise the nil-host path, leaving the new parsing/guard behavior untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] website_name returns nil for website values that URI.parse rejects (e.g. legacy data like 'http://exa mple.com/x'), silently hiding the entire globe/link block in user.hbs, whereas the removed client-side code (website.split("/")[2]) still displayed a host for those same values. Any existing profile whose website string is not URI-parseable loses its displayed website link with no error and no log — a silent display regression for legacy data; users with malformed saved websites see the field vanish after deploy.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` does `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early if `website_host.nil?`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The same-site detection is asymmetric: a website on a subdomain of a 2-label instance host (website 'www.example.com', Discourse.current_hostname 'example.com') falls into the else branch, ends_with?(".www.example.com") is false, and the path is dropped, while the mirrored configuration (instance 'forum.example.com', website 'www.example.com') shows the full path via the elsif branch. Users whose site is served at the apex domain get the truncated host-only display for subdomain websites even though the feature's stated purpose ('show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain') and the sibling 3-label case both say the path should be shown — the same logical site renders differently depending on which side holds the subdomain.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the logic is asymmetric: when the instance host is apex (e.g. `example.com`, 2 labels) and the user website is a subdomain (e.g. `www.example.com/user`), it falls into the final `else` and returns only `website_host` because `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is false, dropping the path. The mirrored 3-label case (`forums.example.com` vs `www.example.com`) hits the `elsif` and can return `website_host + path`. This asymmetry is directly present in the diff, but whether subdomain-vs-apex should include the path is not specified by the added tests/comments, so it's best treated as an uncovered edge-case/design gap rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new tests only exercise the website_host == discourse_host branch and the else (ends_with?) branch; the elsif branch (equal label counts > 2, e.g. instance 'forums.example.com' with website 'www.example.com') is never covered. The most convoluted conditional in website_name (the ternary comparing both split('.')[1..-1] suffixes) can regress to always-true or always-false without any test failing, and given the asymmetry bug at serializer lines 141-148 the branch boundary behavior is exactly where a regression is likely.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, there are three branches: `website_host == discourse_host`, the `elsif` for equal dot-label counts with length > 2, and the final `else` using `ends_with?`. The added specs cover (1) `website_host != discourse_host` with 2-label hosts (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`) which goes to the final `else`, (2) the equality branch (`example.com` vs `example.com`), and (3) the final `else` true-path via subdomain (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). No spec exercises the `elsif` case (e.g. `forums.example.com` with website `www.example.com`), leaving that more complex ternary untested.
